newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sega says to open amusement sites in South Korea.
newsitem.headline: Sega says to open amusement sites in South Korea.

text.p: Sega Enterprises Ltd said on Wednesday that it will operate amusement facilities in South Korea through a joint venture with the Seoul-based Lotte group.
Sega plans to open the first site near Seoul by March 1999 and hopes to open a total of 20 sites in the following five years, it said.
A company spokeswoman said the joint venture, owned equally by Sega and the Lotte group, has starting capital of 11 billion won.
Sega estimates the South Korean amusement business to be worth about 10 billion yen a year, compared with 500 billion yen in Japan.
The company said the joint venture, Lotte Sega Co Ltd, aims for sales of about 410 million yen in the 1998/99 business year.
